text:
mike: Heads-up — seeing a sharp increase in preemptions from the preemptible GPU allocator in us-east-1 around 12:07UTC. Lots of tenants falling back to shared pools, p99 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~820ms.

anya: ugh. any evict logs or allocator traces? can you dump the snippet?

mike: pasted the last evict lines below:
```
[12:07:21] allocator: Pod evicted: tenant=t-42 reason=Preemption candidate=spot-gpu-1 node=ip-10-0-7-45 src=spot-allocator
[12:07:21] fallback: route request tenant=t-42 -> shared-pool-alloc (policy=fallback_allow)
[12:07:22] telemetry: shared-pool-util=0.78, p99=0.82s, fallback-rate=0.18
[12:07:25] allocator: preemptible_backoff_ms=0, try_reassign -> eviction cascade
```

ben: looks like a combination of (1) preemptible hysteresis too low, (2) fallback_policy is permissive so we slammed shared pool, and (3) tenant t-42 sent a sustained burst. shared-pool utilization crossed 75% so QoS degraded.

carmen: was this correlated with any deployment or customer job? ops can we identify request path?

mike: it's aligned with a spike to /generate from tenant=t-42 at 12:06:50 — qps ~3x baseline for ~90s. no new deploys in that window.

ops-lead: Proposed mitigations:
- increase preemptible_hysteresis_ms to 30s to avoid mid-stream churn
- change fallback_policy to reject_when_shared_util>0.7 (so heavy tenants get rate-limited rather than move noisy jobs)
- add a short-lived warm pool for heavy-known tenants (dedicated warm slices)

Config patch (canary):
```yaml
allocator:
  preemptible_hysteresis_ms: 30000
  fallback_policy: reject_when_shared_util_gt_0_7
  tenant_burst_protection: true
```

infra-bot: autoscaler: added 4 nodes to shared-pool-us-east-1 at 12:08:00 to relieve pressure (scale-up triggered by shared-pool-util > 0.75).

anya: plan: apply canary config to us-east-1a now, monitor 30m for fallback-rate and p99. if stable, roll to all us-east. also add temporary tenant throttle for t-42. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ben: +1. i'll add an alert: fallback-rate > 2% in 5m AND tenant burst qps > 2000 => page oncall. also recommend we create a warm-dedicated reservation for top-10 bursty tenants to avoid this next quarter.

carmen: can we also capture a per-tenant cost delta when fallback happens? we should charge a different unit or notify customers when they hit fallback routing.

mike: sounds good. i'll push the canary and attach Grafana links once metrics stabilize. thanks folks. :thumbsup:
